# FRE 902 self-authentication certification (template)

> **What this template is.** A drop-in certification the institution's records custodian signs to self-authenticate FFIEC chain-of-custody electronic evidence in federal proceedings. The template covers FRE 902(13) (records generated by an electronic process or system), 902(14) (data copied from an electronic device, storage medium, or file), and 902(11) (records of regularly conducted activity) as a hash-only variant for cases where the declarant cannot reproduce LLM input/output but can prove the chain's integrity. The certification is written so a federal AUSA, defense counsel, or institution legal team in any U.S. district can drop it into a discovery production with only the marked fields to fill in.

## How to use this template

1. **Pick the variant.** Three certification blocks are provided:
   - **§A — FRE 902(13) certification** for records produced by the chain SDK / verifier as a regularly relied-upon electronic process.
   - **§B — FRE 902(14) certification** for the byte-faithful copy of chain entries handed to opposing counsel (the "snapshot manifest" variant).
   - **§C — FRE 902(11) hash-only certification** for the case where the declarant cannot reproduce the LLM's input/output but can prove the chain's integrity from the seal record forward.
2. **Fill in the marked fields.** Every `[INSTITUTION:fillin]` token names a value the declarant supplies before signature. Tokens are explicit so a reviewer or AUSA can scan for unfilled gaps before filing.
3. **The declaration is under penalty of perjury per 28 USC §1746** so the certification is functionally equivalent to a notarized affidavit for federal purposes. Some state-court rules may require notarization separately; the institution's counsel reviews state-rule alignment.
4. **Pair with foundation testimony.** The certification supports self-authentication; live foundation testimony is unnecessary if the certification is unrebutted. If the opposing party rebuts authenticity, the institution's witness lays foundation per `docs/litigation-support.md` §3.
5. **Records by reference.** Each certification names the records by `(tenant_id, run_id, seq)` range plus the daily seal record(s) covering them. The institution provides the records at production; the certification authenticates them.

## Boilerplate preamble (use for all variants)

> The undersigned declarant, [INSTITUTION:fillin — declarant full legal name], having personal knowledge of the matters stated herein, declares under penalty of perjury under the laws of the United States of America (28 U.S.C. § 1746) as follows:

The preamble appears once at the top of the signed declaration. The declarant fills in the variant-specific paragraphs that follow.

## §A — FRE 902(13) certification — electronic process or system

Use this variant when the records the institution produces in discovery were generated, captured, or processed by the chain SDK or the verifier as part of the institution's regularly relied-upon electronic process.

### §A.1 Declarant qualifications

> 1. I am [INSTITUTION:fillin — declarant full legal name], [INSTITUTION:fillin — declarant title], of [INSTITUTION:fillin — institution legal name] (the "Institution"). I have served in this role since [INSTITUTION:fillin — date or duration].
> 2. As part of my duties, I am the records custodian for the chain-of-custody system described below. I have personal knowledge of the system's operation, the records it produces, and the procedures the Institution follows to retain and produce the records.
> 3. I am authorized by the Institution to make this certification on its behalf.

### §A.2 System identification

> 4. The Institution operates an FFIEC chain-of-custody system implemented under the v1.0a normative specification (the "Specification"). The Specification is publicly available at [INSTITUTION:fillin — spec URL or reference].
> 5. The system captures AI-driven decisions in the Institution's regulated workflows. The records consist of:
>    - Per-event chain entries recording the AI's prompts, the AI's responses, the tools the agent invoked, the routing decisions that selected providers, and the Institution's operational state at the moment of decision.
>    - Daily seal records aggregating each tenant-day's events under a Merkle root signed by the Institution's hardware security module ("HSM").
>    - Operational events recording the system's lifecycle (Specification §10.2).
> 6. The system uses the following cryptographic primitives, each NIST-standardized:
>    - HMAC-SHA-256 (FIPS Publication 198-1) for the per-event MAC.
>    - SHA-256 (FIPS Publication 180-4) for the per-event payload hash and the Merkle tree.
>    - Ed25519 (FIPS Publication 186-5; RFC 8032) for the HSM signature on the daily Merkle root.
>    - HKDF-SHA-256 (RFC 5869) for the per-tenant session-key derivation.
>    - JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785) for the canonical-form encoding.
>    - RFC 6962 Merkle aggregation for the daily seal.

### §A.3 Process description

> 7. The chain-of-custody system was operating in the regular course of the Institution's business when the records were captured. The Institution relies on the records in the ordinary course of operating the AI workflows the records describe.
> 8. The records were produced as part of the system's normal operation. They were not created in anticipation of litigation or for the purpose of this proceeding.
> 9. The system's procedures include:
>    - Per-event capture of AI activity into the chain at the moment of decision (Specification §4.1).
>    - Daily aggregation of the day's events into a Merkle root and signature by the Institution's HSM (Specification §4.2, §4.3).
>    - Retention of the records for the longer of the Institution's documented retention period or seven years (Specification §10.9, §10.13).
>    - Periodic verification of chain integrity by running the verifier per Specification §7 (the "Verification Procedure").
> 10. Personnel authorized to operate the system are documented in the Institution's control description. The signing-key custody is held by personnel with `sign`-only authorization on the HSM, separated from personnel with HSM administrative access (Specification §10.5).

### §A.4 Integrity verification method

> 11. The Verification Procedure is a 12-step ordered procedure that re-executes against retained ledger artifacts. Each step rejects a different attack class with a normative byte-for-byte failure-reason string.
> 12. The Verification Procedure was executed against the records produced in this proceeding on [INSTITUTION:fillin — verifier-run date]. The verifier produced exit code [INSTITUTION:fillin — exit code: 0 = PASS, 1 = FAIL, 2 = structural error, 3 = configuration error] and reported [INSTITUTION:fillin — three-line normative output for FAIL: `Status: FAIL`, `Step: N`, `Reason: <text>`; or `Status: PASS` for PASS; or `Status: PASS-STRUCTURALLY, key-bound verification skipped` for witness-mode PASS].
> 13. The verifier binary used to perform the Verification Procedure has the following identifiers:
>    - Binary SHA-256: `[INSTITUTION:fillin — 64-character lowercase hex SHA-256 of the verifier binary]`.
>    - SLSA build provenance attestation: [INSTITUTION:fillin — Sigstore Rekor inclusion proof URL or content-addressed reference].
>    - Source-of-truth identifier: [INSTITUTION:fillin — Git commit hash or signed artifact reference].
> 14. The verifier-run was recorded as a `verifier.run_completed` operational event in the chain itself. The event carries the verifier's binary SHA-256, the operator identity, the host, and the result. The event is itself integrity-bound under the chain's per-event MAC and the daily seal that includes it.

### §A.5 Records identification

> 15. The records this certification authenticates are the chain entries and seal records identified in [INSTITUTION:fillin — Schedule A or production manifest reference], specifically:
>    - **Tenant identifier(s).** `[INSTITUTION:fillin — list of tenant_id values]`.
>    - **Run identifier(s) and sequence ranges.** `[INSTITUTION:fillin — list of (run_id, seq_start..seq_end) tuples]`.
>    - **Date range.** `[INSTITUTION:fillin — UTC start date]` through `[INSTITUTION:fillin — UTC end date]`.
>    - **Seal records.** `[INSTITUTION:fillin — list of (tenant_id, seal_date) for the seals covering the runs above]`.
> 16. The records are produced in two byte-faithful forms (the "captured JSON" form and the "canonical bytes" form), as contemplated by Federal Rule of Evidence 1001(d) and 1003. Both forms are produced; both are originals as defined in the Specification §5.2.
> 17. The Institution's public-key fingerprint for the signing-key under which the seal records are signed is `[INSTITUTION:fillin — 16-byte fingerprint as 32-character lowercase hex]`. The corresponding public key is registered in [INSTITUTION:fillin — public-key registry URL or institution-controlled location].

### §A.6 Specification-conformant procedural compliance

> 18. The records were produced by an implementation of the Specification that, at the time of capture, was conformant with the Specification's normative requirements, including:
>    - The HSM custody requirement (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or higher), Specification §10.5.
>    - The append-only enforcement at the application and database role layers, Specification §10.3.
>    - The IKM minimum-length requirement (32 bytes), Specification §10.6, and the IKM-generation CSPRNG provenance, Specification §10.6.1.
>    - The constant-time comparison discipline for MAC and fingerprint checks, Specification §10.8.
>    - The OTLP transport over TLS 1.3 (or, where the §5.1 sunset clause applies, TLS 1.2 under documented exception), Specification §5.1.
>    - **Pre-MAC redaction discipline** per Specification §10.22 (Round-17 CFPB-P2): where the records contain redacted fields, the redaction was applied at the SDK boundary before the per-event MAC sealed the canonical bytes; the chain entry's `audit.redaction.*` attribute family records the policy_id, policy_version, redacted_field_paths, redaction_method, and disposition for each redacted entry. [honors §10.22]
> 19. The Institution maintains a vendor-conformance attestation confirming the implementation passes the FFIEC conformance corpus per `docs/vendor-conformance-attestation.md` (where applicable to the Institution's deployment topology). The current attestation reference is [INSTITUTION:fillin — attestation ID and registry URL].

> **Technical Notes — pre-MAC redaction discipline (§10.22).** "Pre-MAC" means redaction runs at the SDK before the cryptographic seal binds the bytes; "post-MAC" would mean redacting after the seal, which is non-conformant under §10.22 unless the redacted form lives on a separate child chain that anchors back to a parent unredacted chain via the §10.21 cross-anchor mechanism. In practice the certification's load-bearing point is that the captured JSON form (§5.2) IS the redacted form — a CFPB or state-DOI examiner reading the chain alone cannot reproduce a decision driver that was redacted, and the `audit.redaction.*` attributes let the examiner detect that fact mechanically rather than inferring it from architecture.

### §A.7 Declaration and signature (FRE 902(13))

> 20. The records identified above are the original or duplicate records of the Institution's chain-of-custody system, produced by an electronic process or system, that produces an accurate result.
> 21. I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the United States of America that the foregoing is true and correct.

```
Executed on _____________________________, 20___, in [INSTITUTION:fillin — city, state].

Signature: ________________________________

Printed name: [INSTITUTION:fillin — declarant full legal name]
Title: [INSTITUTION:fillin — declarant title]
Institution: [INSTITUTION:fillin — institution legal name]
Email: [INSTITUTION:fillin — declarant email]
Phone: [INSTITUTION:fillin — declarant phone]
```

## §B — FRE 902(14) certification — electronic copy authenticated by digital identification

Use this variant when the records the institution produces in discovery are byte-faithful copies of chain entries from the institution's storage. This variant is the bytes-as-handed-over authentication; the snapshot manifest names every file in the export bundle plus its SHA-256.

### §B.1 Declarant qualifications

I have personal knowledge of the records described below and the procedure by which the records were copied from the Institution's storage media for production in this proceeding.

### §B.2 Records identification

> 2. The records this certification authenticates are the chain-of-custody export bundle delivered to [INSTITUTION:fillin — receiving party] on [INSTITUTION:fillin — production date]. The bundle is identified as [INSTITUTION:fillin — production identifier or bates range].

| [INSTITUTION:fillin — file path] | `[INSTITUTION:fillin — 64-char hex]` | [INSTITUTION:fillin — description] |

> 4. The bundle's snapshot manifest, identified as [INSTITUTION:fillin — manifest filename, e.g., `snapshot-manifest.json`], is signed by the Institution's HSM under Ed25519 (FIPS 186-5; RFC 8032). The manifest's signature artifact is [INSTITUTION:fillin — signature filename, e.g., `snapshot-manifest.json.sig`]. The manifest's content digest is `[INSTITUTION:fillin — 64-char SHA-256 hex of the canonical-form manifest]`.

### §B.3 Copy procedure

> 5. The records were copied from the Institution's storage as follows:
>    - Storage location: [INSTITUTION:fillin — DB / object-store / file-system identifier].
>    - Copy date and time: [INSTITUTION:fillin — RFC 3339 UTC timestamp].

### §B.4 Hash verification

> 7. Each file in the bundle has been hashed under SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4). The hash table in §B.2 above is the result of that hashing.
> 8. A reviewer of this certification may independently compute the SHA-256 of any file in the bundle and compare against the hash recorded in §B.2. A match is the digital identification that authenticates the file under FRE 902(14).

The chain-of-custody system's integrity properties are as described in §A.2 and §A.6 of the §A FRE 902(13) certification (or in the underlying Specification if §A is not paired with this certification).
> 11. The Verification Procedure (Specification §7) was executed against the records in the bundle on [INSTITUTION:fillin — verifier-run date]; the verifier produced exit code [INSTITUTION:fillin — exit code] and reported [INSTITUTION:fillin — three-line normative output].

### §B.6 Declaration and signature (FRE 902(14))

> 12. The records identified above are byte-faithful copies of records held in the Institution's storage. Each record is authenticated by a process of digital identification — namely, the SHA-256 hash recorded in this certification, computed at the time of copy and recoverable by any reviewer on demand.

## §C — FRE 902(11) hash-only certification — regularly conducted activity

Use this variant when the institution cannot reproduce the LLM's substantive input or output (the underlying API call to the provider, the model's token stream) but can authenticate the chain's record of what the institution received. This is the load-bearing variant for cases where:

- The provider has retired the model and the underlying inference is not reproducible.
- The institution's data-classification policy excludes the substantive prompt or response from the chain (only the hash and operational metadata are retained).
- The institution can prove the chain's seal record covers the period without reconstructing the underlying inference.

### §C.1 Declarant qualifications

> 1. I am [INSTITUTION:fillin — declarant full legal name], [INSTITUTION:fillin — declarant title], of [INSTITUTION:fillin — institution legal name] (the "Institution"). I am the records custodian for the records identified in §C.4 below.

### §C.2 Records and limitation of scope

> 2. The records this certification authenticates are the chain entries and seal records covering the period from [INSTITUTION:fillin — UTC start date] through [INSTITUTION:fillin — UTC end date] for tenant identifier(s) [INSTITUTION:fillin — list of tenant_id values].
> 3. **Scope limitation.** This certification authenticates the chain's record of what the Institution received from the AI provider and recorded under the chain's integrity primitives. This certification does NOT authenticate the substantive content of any specific prompt or response, because [INSTITUTION:fillin — reason: e.g., "the provider has retired the model; the inference is not reproducible" or "the Institution's data classification policy required exclusion of customer PII from the recorded prompt and response, and only the SHA-256 hash of those values is retained"].
> 4. The Institution does NOT, by this certification, attest to:
>    - The factual accuracy of any AI statement.
>    - The compliance of any AI statement with the Institution's policy.
>    - The freedom of any AI statement from bias.
>    These are excluded by the epistemic scope of the chain (Specification §1.2).

### §C.3 Regularly conducted activity (FRE 803(6))

> 5. The records were made at or near the time of the events they describe, by — or from information transmitted by — someone with knowledge.
> 6. The records were kept in the course of the Institution's regularly conducted activity. Operating an FFIEC chain-of-custody record of AI-driven decisions is a regular activity of the Institution because:
>    - [INSTITUTION:fillin — institutional rationale: e.g., "Federal regulations require the Institution to maintain a chain of custody for AI-driven decisions in adverse-action workflows"; or "The Institution's risk-management policy requires the records as part of its model-risk-management program under SR 11-7"; or other institution-specific rationale].
> 7. Making the records was a regular practice of the regularly conducted activity. The chain-of-custody system was always operating during the period; every AI decision in scope produced a chain entry.

### §C.4 Integrity verification

> 8. The Verification Procedure (Specification §7) was executed against the records on [INSTITUTION:fillin — verifier-run date]. The verifier produced exit code [INSTITUTION:fillin — exit code] and reported [INSTITUTION:fillin — three-line normative output].
> 9. The verifier confirmed:
>    - Per-event MAC verification PASSED (or PASSED-STRUCTURALLY in witness mode) for every chain entry in the period.
>    - Daily Merkle root recomputation matched the sealed root for every tenant-day in the period.
>    - HSM signature verification PASSED for every seal record in the period.
> 10. Where the verifier produced PASS-WITH-ANOMALY findings (late-binding entries, cadence anomalies, structural-only PASS under witness mode), the anomalies are itemized in [INSTITUTION:fillin — anomaly schedule reference]; each is dispositioned per the Institution's IR procedure and is not material to chain integrity.

### §C.5 Hash-only authentication — what the records prove

> 11. By the SHA-256 hashes recorded on each chain entry's `payload_hash` field and the HSM signature on each daily seal record's Merkle root:
>    - **The Institution received the bytes whose hash is recorded** at the time recorded.
>    - **No alteration of the recorded bytes occurred between capture and verification.**
> 12. A reviewer who has the substantive prompt or response in another form (a separately-retained provider-side log, a downstream system that mirrored the response) can verify whether that form's bytes produce the SHA-256 hash recorded in the chain. A match is the digital identification that the Institution received those bytes.

### §C.6 Declaration and signature (FRE 902(11))

> 13. The records identified above are records of regularly conducted activity, kept in the regular course of the Institution's business. The chain's integrity primitives prove the records have not been altered from capture to production.
> 14. I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the United States of America that the foregoing is true and correct.

## §D — Self-authentication block for the seal record (companion sub-block)

Use this block when the seal record is the load-bearing artifact and the AUSA wants a separately-citable self-authentication of just the seal. This block can be appended to §A or §C, or used standalone.

> The seal record identified as `(tenant_id = [INSTITUTION:fillin — tenant_id], seal_date = [INSTITUTION:fillin — UTC date])` is reproduced below in canonical form. The HSM signature on the record is `[INSTITUTION:fillin — base64-encoded Ed25519 signature]`. The signing-key public-key fingerprint is `[INSTITUTION:fillin — 16-byte fingerprint as 32-char hex]`.
>
> Verification of the signature against the public key whose fingerprint is recorded above will confirm:
> - The Merkle root over the day's events is `[INSTITUTION:fillin — 64-char SHA-256 hex]`.
> - The seal was produced under HSM custody at FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or higher.
> - The seal record has not been altered since the moment of signing.
>
> A reviewer recomputes the Merkle root from the day's chain entries (per Specification §4.2 / RFC 6962) and compares against the sealed root above; a match is the cryptographic confirmation that the chain entries are the entries the seal covers.

## §E — Self-authentication block for an extracted entry (companion sub-block)

Use this block when a single chain entry is the load-bearing artifact (e.g., the AI's response to a specific customer interaction). This block can be appended to §A or §B, or used standalone.

> The chain entry identified as `(tenant_id = [INSTITUTION:fillin — tenant_id], run_id = [INSTITUTION:fillin — run_id], seq = [INSTITUTION:fillin — seq])` is reproduced below in both forms:
>
> **Captured JSON form (content-bearing).** [INSTITUTION:fillin — captured JSON of the entry, paste verbatim].
>
> **Canonical bytes form (integrity-bearing, RFC 8785).** SHA-256 of canonical bytes: `[INSTITUTION:fillin — 64-char SHA-256 hex of canonical bytes]`. (The canonical bytes themselves are reproducible from the captured JSON form per RFC 8785.)
>
> The entry's `payload_hash` is `[INSTITUTION:fillin — 64-char hex]`. The entry's `key_fingerprint` is `[INSTITUTION:fillin — 32-char hex]`.
>
> The day's seal record (covering the entry's `captured_at` date) is reproduced in §D above (or separately at [INSTITUTION:fillin — reference]). The Merkle inclusion proof for this entry against the sealed Merkle root is reproduced at [INSTITUTION:fillin — proof reference]; the proof is verifiable per RFC 6962 §2.1.1.
>
> Verification of the per-event MAC against the institution's session key, plus verification of the Merkle inclusion proof against the sealed root, plus verification of the HSM signature on the seal record, proves the entry was a member of the day's sealed set and has not been altered since capture.

## §F — Verifier exit-code reference (companion table)

This table is reproduced verbatim from Specification §10.12 to support the AUSA's review of the verifier output cited in §A.4 / §B.5 / §C.4.

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | PASS or PASS-STRUCTURALLY (witness mode). The verifier completed and the chain (or the structural subset under witness mode) verified. |
| 1 | FAIL. The chain failed integrity verification at one of the §7 steps. The reason and step number appear on stdout per the normative output format. |
| 2 | Structural / input error. The verifier could not begin the §7 procedure: file unreadable, JSON malformed, mandatory header field missing entirely, or file empty. |
| 3 | Configuration error. The verifier was invoked without a required argument, the algorithm is unknown, or the posture flag does not match the chain's posture. |

A `0` exit code with `Status: PASS` is an unambiguous integrity confirmation. A `0` exit code with `Status: PASS-STRUCTURALLY, key-bound verification skipped` is a witness-mode confirmation — structural integrity verified, key-bound verification deferred (the IKM was not provided, typically because the examiner is operating under the regulator-trust boundary). A `1` exit code is an integrity finding the institution must disposition before proceeding. Exit codes `2` and `3` are deployment / configuration problems, NOT integrity findings.

## §G — Notes for AUSAs and counsel

### When to attach §A vs §B vs §C

- **§A FRE 902(13)** is the right choice when the records are the substantive output of the chain SDK and the institution can describe the regular electronic process that produced them. This is the most common variant.
- **§B FRE 902(14)** is the right choice when the question is "are these the bytes the institution holds?" — i.e., the bytes-as-handed-over question. Use §B when opposing counsel may challenge the production's faithfulness to the institution's storage.
- **§C FRE 902(11)** is the right choice when the institution cannot reproduce the LLM input/output substantively but can prove the chain's record of what the institution received. This variant is the load-bearing fall-back for retired-model and PII-classification cases.

The variants are not mutually exclusive. A complete production may attach §A (the regular process produced the records), §B (these specific bytes are byte-faithful copies), and §C as an alternative authentication theory the AUSA invokes if the §A or §B variant is challenged.

### Pairing with foundation testimony

A FRE 902 certification is self-executing if unrebutted. If opposing counsel files a notice of intent to challenge authenticity, the institution's records custodian (the declarant) testifies live to lay foundation. The certification's content provides the witness's roadmap; the witness should review `docs/litigation-support.md` §3 (foundation-testimony framework) before testimony.

### Notice requirement for FRE 902(11), 902(13), 902(14)

Each rule requires the proponent to give the adverse party reasonable written notice of the intent to offer the record and to make the record and certification available for inspection. The notice procedure is:

1. The proponent serves the adverse party with the certification AND the records (or a manifest naming them) at least [INSTITUTION:fillin — district-specific notice period; FRE default is "before the trial or hearing"].
2. The adverse party has the inspection period to challenge authenticity.
3. If the adverse party does not challenge, the certification is admitted without live foundation.
4. If the adverse party challenges, the institution's witness lays foundation per §G above.

### When the verifier reports exit code 1 (FAIL)

A FAIL result is NOT a reason to withhold the certification. The certification states what the verifier found; if the records FAIL verification, the certification reports the FAIL exit code, the step number, and the normative reason string. An AUSA in possession of a FAIL certification has unambiguous evidence of an integrity finding; the disposition of the FAIL is a separate question (institution IR procedure, possible spoliation analysis under FRCP 37(e), production of the institution's IR record alongside the FAIL certification).

The certification's truthfulness is the load-bearing requirement. Producing a misleading PASS certification when the verifier reported FAIL is perjury under 28 USC §1746.

### Witness-mode verification in regulator hand-offs

When the institution does not transmit the IKM to the receiving party (typical for a federal investigator who has not separately compelled disclosure), the verifier operates in witness mode and produces `Status: PASS-STRUCTURALLY, key-bound verification skipped`. This is a legitimate authentication path — the structural integrity, the Merkle root, and the HSM signature are all verified; the per-event MAC is NOT verified because the IKM was not provided.

A witness-mode PASS plus a §A certification is admissible under FRE 901(b)(9) (process or system that produces an accurate result) and FRE 902(13). Opposing counsel may challenge witness-mode authentication on the theory that the per-event MACs were not verified; the institution's witness rebuts by noting the cross-tenant binding (HKDF info parameter), the seal-level MAC binding via the Merkle root, and the HSM signature's coverage of the root. The Daubert "Known error rate" answer (Specification §1.1) is the load-bearing rebuttal.

### Cross-border holdings and MLAT

When the records are held in non-U.S. regions (per Specification §10.15 multi-region resilience), the institution's records custodian declares this in the certification and notes the MLAT or Hague Evidence Convention basis under which the records were retrieved for production. The certification is silent on whether the cross-border retrieval was authorized; that is a separate question for the AUSA's office and the institution's legal team.

## §H — Declaration form (clean copy for signature)

The clean copy below combines the variants into a single form the declarant fills in. Variants not applicable are deleted before signature.

## Summary

This certification template gives the institution's records custodian three pre-drafted variants for self-authenticating FFIEC chain-of-custody electronic evidence in federal proceedings: FRE 902(13) for records produced by a regularly relied-upon electronic process, FRE 902(14) for byte-faithful copies of records authenticated by SHA-256, and FRE 902(11) for hash-only authentication where the substantive AI input/output is not reproducible. Each variant is signed under penalty of perjury per 28 USC §1746. The declarations cite the spec sections an AUSA or defense expert will recognize, and the verifier exit-code reference table supports the AUSA's review of the verifier output the certification cites.

The institution paste-completes the marked fields, deletes the inapplicable variants and sub-blocks, and the result is admissible without live foundation testimony — provided the adverse party does not challenge authenticity. If they do, the institution's witness lays foundation per `docs/litigation-support.md` §3 with the certification as the witness's roadmap.

Naveed G-1 (and N-6) closure: the template covers FRE 902(11), 902(13), 902(14), names the verifier exit codes per Specification §10.12, identifies the records by `(tenant_id, run_id, seq)` range, names the verifier binary's SHA-256 and SLSA attestation, attests regular-course-of-business per FRE 803(6), and is signed under penalty of perjury per 28 USC §1746. AUSAs in any U.S. district can drop this template into a discovery production with only the marked fields to fill in.

# Addendum — Adversarial-balance protections

> **What this addendum is.** A set of additional template provisions and procedural commitments the institution makes when the certification is being introduced into adversarial litigation — most commonly class-action consumer litigation, opposing-counsel-discovery contexts, or any matter where the opposing party is expected to mount an authenticity challenge under FRE 901, a foundation challenge under 902(13), or a Daubert challenge under FRE 702. The base template at §A-§G above is sufficient for unopposed introductions and for most criminal-side selective production. This addendum sharpens three load-bearing points opposing counsel will press against — declarant independence from the verifier-run, customer-side verification access, and witness-mode foundation. *(closes Hartwell G-1, G-2, G-6)*

> **What this addendum is NOT.** Not a replacement for the base template variants. The institution adopts the base variant that fits the production (§A 902(13) for regularly-relied-upon process, §B 902(14) for byte-faithful copy, §C 902(11) for hash-only) and then layers the addendum's provisions where the matter's adversarial posture warrants. The institution's outside counsel decides which addendum provisions to include based on the specific litigation context.

## Addendum A1 — Declarant-independence provisions

The base §A.1 declarant qualifications name the records custodian as the declarant. Nothing in §A.1 requires the declarant to be different from the person who ran the verifier, configured the master-key flag, controlled the files the verifier read, or had write access to the IKM registry. In adversarial litigation, opposing counsel will press the question: "Did you run the verifier yourself? If not, who did, and were they reporting to you? Did anyone outside your reporting line independently re-run the verifier against the same bytes?" The institution's certification posture under base §A is exposed to the foundation challenge that the declarant is the same person (or in the same reporting line) as the operator of every component the certification rests on.

The addendum closes this gap with a four-element independence commitment.

### Addendum A1.1 — Independent verifier-runner identification

> **Add to §A.4 paragraph 12:** The Verifier Procedure was executed by [INSTITUTION:fillin — verifier-runner full legal name and title]. The verifier-runner [check applicable]:
>
> - [ ] is the same individual as the declarant
> - [ ] reports to the declarant within the institution's reporting structure
> - [ ] is independent of the declarant's reporting line (separate functional reporting up to a different senior officer)
> - [ ] is external to the institution (named below in Addendum A1.2)

The four-element check makes the verifier-runner's relationship to the declarant explicit and on the record before opposing counsel asks. The declarant signs the certification with the relationship documented; opposing counsel cannot manufacture a foundation challenge from ambiguity.

### Addendum A1.2 — External verifier-runner option

When the litigation context warrants additional independence, the institution arranges for an external verifier-runner. Three external-verifier-runner postures are commonly available.

| Posture | Verifier-runner | Use case |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Institution's external SOC 2 audit firm | The audit firm's engagement team runs the verifier under their National Office independence procedure (cross-reference `audit-procedures.md` §3 SOC 2 sampling) | Highest-credibility posture for class-action defense; the firm's National Office maintains a separate public-key registry snapshot |
| (b) Court-appointed neutral expert | Counsel petitions the court for a Rule 706 neutral expert who runs the verifier on behalf of the bench | Useful when both parties stipulate to an independent verifier-run |
| (c) Regulator-side examination team | The institution's primary federal supervisor or NYDFS examination team runs the verifier as part of an examination cycle; the institution receives the verifier output as part of the examination record | Available where an examination is open during the litigation period |

The certification's §A.4 paragraph 12 names the external verifier-runner, the date of the run, and the runner's public reference (audit firm name, court order reference, examination cycle reference). The chain's `verifier.run_completed` operational event records the external runner's identity in the integrity-bound chain itself.

### Addendum A1.3 — Re-verification by independent party commitment

> **Add to §A.4 paragraph 14:** The Institution commits to permitting independent re-verification of the records produced in this proceeding by any of the following on request:
>
> - The opposing party's expert under a protective-order arrangement governing IKM access (cross-reference Addendum A2 below)
> - The court-appointed neutral expert if one is appointed
> - The Institution's external SOC 2 audit firm under their National Office procedure
>
> The Institution will not assert that the verifier's normative byte-for-byte output is contingent on the Institution's running of the verifier; the verifier's output is reproducible by any party with the same bytes, the same public-key registry snapshot, and the same verifier binary identified in §A.4 paragraph 13.

The commitment is binding on the institution. Opposing counsel cannot challenge the certification's foundation by arguing the verifier is a closed system the institution exclusively controls; the verifier is reproducible by definition, and the institution stipulates to that fact in writing.

### Addendum A1.4 — Verifier-run separation-of-duties attestation

> **Add to §A.4 paragraph 14:** I attest that the verifier-run named in §A.4 paragraph 12 was performed under separation-of-duties discipline. The verifier-runner did NOT have any of the following privileges during the verifier-run:
>
> - HSM administrative access to the signing key
> - Write access to the chain's append-only ledger
> - Write access to the IKM registry
> - Write access to the public-key registry that authoritatively names the seal-signing key

The discipline is the operational expression of the §1.4 compositional security argument. The verifier-runner has read-only access to the artifacts the verifier consumes; the runner has no write authority over any artifact the run depends on. Opposing counsel pressing the "could the runner have tampered with the bytes before running the verifier?" question receives a documented "no" backed by the institution's separation-of-duties roster.

## Addendum A2 — Customer-side verification path with court-controlled IKM escrow

The base template at §G "Witness-mode verification in regulator hand-offs" admits witness mode as an authentication path when the IKM is not transmitted. In adversarial litigation against a class-action plaintiff, witness mode by itself is insufficient — the plaintiff's expert needs an independent authentication path that does not run through the institution's HSM. *(closes Hartwell G-2, G-6)*

The customer-dispute procedures document at `customer-dispute-procedures.md` describes two acceptable shapes for IKM access: (1) court-issued protective order, (2) HSM-mediated verification through the bank's HSM API. Option 2 is the bank's preferred path because the institution controls the verification infrastructure. Option 1 — the court-controlled escrow — is the load-bearing independence path for adversarial litigation.

### Addendum A2.1 — Court-controlled IKM escrow provision

> **Add to §G or as a standalone declaration when the production is to opposing counsel's expert under protective order:** The Institution commits to lodging the IKM material covering the records produced in this proceeding into court-controlled escrow under a Rule 26(c) protective order on the request of any party. The escrow's operational shape:
>
> - The IKM material is delivered to the court clerk or a designated escrow agent under sealed conditions.
> - Opposing counsel's designated expert receives access to the IKM material under the protective order's sealed-access conditions.
> - The expert's access does NOT require running through the Institution's HSM API; the expert may run the verifier independently in full-key mode against the records produced.
> - The Institution does not rate-limit, refuse, or otherwise constrain the expert's verifier runs; the expert may run the verifier as many times as the protective order permits.
>
> The protective order's specific conditions are negotiated by the parties and the court; the Institution stipulates that the IKM material's escrow is acceptable in lieu of HSM-mediated verification when the litigation context warrants.

### Addendum A2.2 — HSM-mediated verification as fallback

When the parties cannot agree on a court-controlled escrow, HSM-mediated verification is the fallback. Under HSM-mediated verification, the institution's HSM dispatches session keys for the verifier on demand, and the expert's verifier runs query the HSM over a documented API. The institution's commitment in this fallback shape:

> **Add to §G when HSM-mediated verification is the fallback:** Where the IKM material is not lodged in court-controlled escrow and the verification is HSM-mediated, the Institution commits to:
>
> - Provide the expert with documented API endpoints the expert's verifier can query for session keys
> - Not rate-limit the expert's queries below the rate the institution's own production verifier runs at
> - Log every query in the chain's operational-event stream as a `verifier.run_started` and `verifier.run_completed` pair, with the expert's identity attributed
> - Provide the operational-event log covering the expert's queries to the expert and to opposing counsel on request, in integrity-bound form
> - Not refuse run identifiers as "expired" or dispatch alternate session keys; queries return the session keys the chain produced at capture time
>
> The Institution acknowledges that HSM-mediated verification places the Institution in the verification path. The Institution further acknowledges that opposing counsel may argue this constitutes a less-independent verification posture than court-controlled escrow; the Institution does not contest that characterization.

The acknowledgment is on the record. The institution's commitment to documented API endpoints and integrity-bound query logs makes the HSM-mediated path verifiable rather than opaque; opposing counsel pressing "the bank's HSM is a black box" receives the integrity-bound query log as the rebuttal.

### Addendum A2.3 — Regulator-in-the-loop verification path

The third independence path: regulator-in-the-loop verification. The institution's primary federal supervisor or state cybersecurity supervisor (NYDFS Cybersecurity Division, OCC examination team, FRB examination team) runs the verifier under their examination authority, and the verifier output is shared with both the institution and opposing counsel.

> **Add to §G when regulator-in-the-loop verification is invoked:** The Institution requested or received a regulator-conducted verifier-run as part of the [INSTITUTION:fillin — examination cycle reference] examination. The verifier-run was conducted by [INSTITUTION:fillin — regulator examination team identifier] on [INSTITUTION:fillin — date]. The regulator's verifier output is attached as Exhibit [INSTITUTION:fillin — exhibit number] and is independently authenticated by the regulator's signature on the examination record.

The regulator's verifier-run output is a separate authentication path that does not depend on the institution's witness; opposing counsel pressing the "the bank controls all three layers" theory receives the regulator's independently-conducted output as rebuttal.

## Addendum A3 — Witness-mode foundation reinforcement

The base §G admits witness mode plus 902(13) as a cross-examinable foundation. When the litigation context anticipates a witness-mode-coverage challenge, the addendum reinforces the foundation. *(closes Hartwell G-6)*

### Addendum A3.1 — Three-layer rebuttal articulation

> **Add to §G paragraph 3:** The Institution's compositional security argument under Specification §1.4 establishes that the chain's integrity claim rests on three independent detection layers — the per-event MAC under per-tenant HKDF-derived session keys, the daily Merkle root binding the day's events into a single integrity-bound aggregate, and the HSM-bound Ed25519 signature over the Merkle root. Witness mode runs the second and third layers (Merkle root recomputation and signature verification) without running the first (per-event MAC verification). The integrity claim under witness mode is therefore that:
>
> - The seal record was produced by the Institution's HSM under FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or higher custody (Specification §10.5)
> - The Merkle root the seal commits to is the root of the chain entries presented (RFC 6962 reconstruction)
> - The chain entries presented have not been altered since sealing (the Merkle root would not match if they had been)
>
> What witness mode does NOT independently authenticate is the per-event binding to the Institution's tenant-specific IKM. The Institution acknowledges that an entry's body could in principle be modified before sealing without witness mode detecting it; the Institution's defense against this scenario is the cross-tenant binding via HKDF info parameter (Specification §4.1), the seal-level MAC binding via the Merkle root (Specification §4.2), and the HSM signature's coverage of the root (Specification §4.3).

The articulation moves the witness-mode foundation from "the spec admits this is a cross-examination angle" to "the institution's witness lays foundation under the three-layer compositional argument with explicit acknowledgment of what witness mode does not do." Opposing counsel's cross-examination has nowhere to go that the institution has not already pre-acknowledged.

### Addendum A3.2 — Independence of the three layers under institutional control

> **Add to §G paragraph 4:** The Institution acknowledges that the three layers in §1.4's compositional security argument are operationally independent in the sense that they are produced by separate procedures — the SDK at capture time produces the per-event MAC, the seal job at end-of-day produces the Merkle root, the HSM produces the signature. The Institution further acknowledges that the three layers are institutionally non-independent in the sense that all three are operated by the same institution. The independence the spec argues for is operational separation-of-duties between roles within the institution (Specification §10.5 HSM custody discipline, Specification §10.6.1 IKM-generation discipline, the chain-operations team versus the HSM administrator versus the records officer).
>
> Opposing counsel may argue that operational separation-of-duties is not equivalent to true cryptographic independence; the Institution does not contest that characterization. The Institution's response to that argument is that:
>
> - True cryptographic independence would require multiple HSMs under multiple custodial parties; that is the architecture for cross-institution multi-signature schemes, not for single-institution chain-of-custody
> - The Institution's separation-of-duties roster, the HSM custody attestation, and the IKM-generation provenance are documented; opposing counsel has access to all three through discovery
> - The independence claim under §1.4 is the strongest claim a single-institution chain can make; opposing counsel arguing for stronger independence is arguing for a different system architecture, not for a defect in this one

The pre-acknowledgment defuses the cross-examination's most effective angle — "the bank controls all three layers." The institution agrees as a matter of fact and explains why the documented separation-of-duties is the strongest available structure. Opposing counsel's argument shifts from "the institution is hiding institutional control" to "the institution should have a different architecture" — a policy argument the bench is unlikely to credit.

## Addendum A4 — When to use this addendum

| Litigation context | Addendum A1 | Addendum A2 | Addendum A3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Criminal selective production under 2703(d) order | Optional | Not applicable (court bound) | Optional |
| Government investigation under examination authority | Optional | Optional | Optional |
| Civil discovery in commercial litigation | Recommended | Recommended | Optional |
| Class-action consumer litigation (RESPA, TILA, ECOA, data-breach) | Required | Required | Required |
| Regulatory enforcement action | Recommended | Optional | Recommended |
| FOIA-driven third-party disclosure | Optional | Not applicable | Optional |
| Internal investigation feeding regulator notification | Optional | Not applicable | Optional |

The institution's outside counsel makes the call on which addendum provisions to include for a specific matter. The addendum provisions are additive to the base template; the base template at §A-§G remains the load-bearing certification text, and the addendum sharpens the foundation in the contexts where adversarial pressure is anticipated.

When the addendum is included in a certification, the certification's clean copy at §H records which addendum provisions were adopted. This becomes part of the certification's documentary record and is preserved in the institution's evidentiary-artifacts retention per spec §10.13.

The record is part of the integrity-bound certification. Opposing counsel inspecting the certification sees not only what the institution attested to but also which adversarial protections the institution adopted for this specific matter.

## §D — Adversarial-balance addendum (optional)

Use this addendum when the certification accompanies a production made on the adverse party's discovery demand (FRCP 34) rather than on the institution's own initiative. The addendum closes three asymmetric-evidence concerns a plaintiff-side expert or a consumer-side counsel will raise: independence of the declarant, completeness of the chain-of-control disclosure, and independence of the verifier-run that produced the certified output. The addendum is deliberately written so the same paragraphs apply whether the production responds to a U.S. class-action subpoena, a GDPR Article 15 disclosure to a data subject, or a cross-border representative-action production under Directive 2020/1828.

### §D.1 Independence-of-declarant attestation

> 28. The declarant attests that the certification above was prepared by the declarant in the declarant's role as records custodian for the Institution. The declarant has not received instruction from the Institution's litigation-defense team, the Institution's outside counsel, the AI vendor, or any other party with an interest in the proceeding to alter the certification's substance. The certification reports the verifier-run's actual output, the spec procedures the Institution actually operates, and the records the Institution actually produced — not a curated subset shaped by the proceeding's adversarial posture.
> 29. The declarant has not been instructed to omit any failure or anomaly the verifier-run surfaced. Any `Status: FAIL`, `Status: PASS-WITH-ANOMALY`, or `Status: PASS-STRUCTURALLY` result the verifier-run produced is reported verbatim in §A.4 (or the analogous variant section) above; the institution's interpretation of any anomaly under `regulator-pack/finding-language.md` is reported alongside the verifier output, not in place of it.
> 30. The declarant has personal authority to execute this certification and is not signing on behalf of an undisclosed principal whose interest in the proceeding the declarant does not disclose.

### §D.2 Chain-of-control disclosure clause

> 31. The Institution discloses its chain-of-control posture for the records this certification authenticates:
>     - The Institution holds the per-tenant master HMAC key (IKM) under HSM custody at [INSTITUTION:fillin — HSM identifier per the verifier output].
>     - The Institution has not transferred the IKM to any third party for the purpose of this proceeding.
>     - The Institution's IKM rotation history during the period covered by the records is preserved per Specification §10.9 and is available for production on the adverse party's request under proportional discovery.
>     - The Institution's daily seal records covering the period have been preserved without modification; the seal records' Merkle roots and HSM signatures are byte-faithful to the records the Institution captured at sealing time.
>     - The verifier-run output reported in §A.4 (or the analogous variant section) reflects the actual state of the records as of the verifier-run date in §A.4. No subsequent modification to the records or the seal records has occurred between the verifier-run date and this certification's signature date.
> 32. If a third party (a vendor-hosted ledger provider, a managed-HSM provider, or a cloud infrastructure provider) operates any part of the chain-of-custody system on behalf of the Institution, the third party's role is named here: [INSTITUTION:fillin — third-party role description, or `none` if the Institution operates its own infrastructure]. The Institution attests that the third party's role does not include modification authority over the records this certification authenticates; the third party's authority is bounded by the Institution's documented service contract.

### §D.3 Verifier-run independence attestation

> 33. The declarant attests that the verifier-run reported in §A.4 was performed by Institution personnel without instruction or assistance from the AI vendor whose model produced any of the records, the vendor whose ledger or HSM hosts the records, or any party adverse to the Institution in the proceeding. The verifier-run's output is the verifier binary's actual exit code and three-line output — not a summary, paraphrase, or institution-edited rendering.
> 34. The verifier binary used was obtained from the project's public release channel under the cosign signature and SLSA build provenance attestation cited in §A.4. The Institution did not modify the verifier binary; the Institution did not configure the verifier in any manner that suppresses the verifier's normative output. The verifier's exit-code semantics per Specification §10.12 are: `0 = PASS`, `1 = FAIL`, `2 = structural error`, `3 = configuration error`. The exit code reported in §A.4 is the actual exit code the verifier emitted.
> 35. The Institution affirms the adverse party's right to obtain the records authenticated here in a form that supports independent verifier-run by the adverse party's expert. The Institution will, on request and within proportional discovery, produce: the on-disk NDJSON form of the certified records (with canonical bytes preserved), the daily seal records covering them, and the resolution of `public_key_id` to the Ed25519 public-key bytes (or a pointer to the Institution's published tenant-key registry resolving the same). The adverse party's expert obtains the verifier binary independently from the project's public release channel; the Institution does not gate access to the verifier binary or the Specification §7 procedure documentation.

### §D.4 When to attach §D

Attach §D when:

- The production responds to an adverse party's discovery demand (FRCP 34, GDPR Article 15, Directive 2020/1828 representative action, or analogous foreign-procedural mechanism).
- The proceeding's procedural posture suggests the adverse party will challenge the institution's evidentiary presentation rather than accept self-authentication.
- The adverse party has indicated, formally or informally, an intent to depose the records custodian or to retain an expert to validate the chain.
- The production is to a national consumer-protection authority (DGCCRF, Verbraucherzentrale, Test-Achats, BEUC, equivalents) or a qualified consumer-protection entity under Directive 2020/1828.

Omit §D when the production is to a U.S. federal regulator under regular-course-of-supervision examination — the regulator's verification posture is grounded in the FFIEC working group's independent review of the spec, and §D's adversarial-balance text would be an awkward addition to a non-adversarial production. The institution's records-custodian and outside counsel jointly decide whether §D belongs in any particular production.
